This module has two parts. First, you present an interactive model in pairs, the explorables session. Then you switch from continuous fields to fully discrete systems: time, space and state all take discrete values. You study elementary cellular automata, the Game of Life and the Nagel-Schreckenberg model of traffic flow [@wolfram1983statistical; @nagel1992cellular].

# Learning Goals

- Explain a published model to your peers, state its assumptions and add an extension, test or criticism of your own.
- Encode an elementary cellular automaton rule as an 8-entry lookup table and simulate it.
- Classify space-time diagrams with the four Wolfram classes and discuss the limits of that classification.
- Explain how boundary conditions and finite lattice size shape long-run behaviour.
- Implement the Game of Life and identify still lifes, oscillators and gliders.
- Implement the Nagel-Schreckenberg rules and estimate the fundamental diagram.
- Decide which model extensions change the fundamental diagram qualitatively.
